Turn a photo into a traceable outline

Start with a clear silhouette, then choose the details that belong in your drawing.

Choose a photo with clear edges

A side profile, a leaf against plain paper, or a cup against a contrasting wall will usually be easier to trace than a subject surrounded by clutter. Look for a clear boundary all the way around the part you want to draw. Crop away distracting objects in your phone’s photo editor before uploading.

Compare Outline and Original

Upload your photo and start in Outline. Move Outline detail down until fine texture recedes, then bring it up just enough to recover landmarks like an eye or a petal seam. Use Original at a low opacity when a soft edge disappears in Outline mode. Switch back to outline whenever you want a clearer guide for crisp edges.

Library drawings already have clean lines. Choose one directly when you want to practice line work without preparing a photo.

Draw in three passes

  1. Silhouette. Start with the largest outer shape. Leave gaps where a shadow or the background makes the edge uncertain.
  2. Landmarks. Add the features that make the subject recognizable, such as a cup handle or the center of a flower.
  3. Details. Add a few texture and shadow lines. Use Hide to compare the drawing on paper with the overlay.

Try a two-minute warm-up

Choose the library’s Oak leaf and trace the silhouette and center vein. Hide the overlay and add the smaller veins by eye. This makes it easier to see which lines you can leave out when tracing a more complex photo.
